889:
You expose the two plans that overlapped that night. Dr. Helena Souza is charged with attempted murder and neural intrusion: the NX-7 and the AR glasses leave no doubt. And Victor Rossi — who climbed the duct, found Arthur paralyzed and dealt the fatal blow with the hydraulic wrench — is arrested for the murder.

The forged chronometer, the lock triggered from the tunnels, the heavy footprints: every piece in place.

Outside, the acid rain finally eases. For the first time in years, the corporation has to admit it: Detective Vance was right.
894:
You named the right man. But without solid evidence — the murder weapon, the forged time, the direct link to the scene — Victor Rossi's corporate lawyers tear the charge apart in under an hour.

Rossi walks out of court smiling, adjusting the glove on his mechanical arm.

Sometimes knowing isn't enough. You have to prove it.
897:
The NX-7 traces are enough to convict Dr. Helena Souza. The corporation celebrates a case closed in record time.

But Arthur was breathing when she disconnected. The blow to the back of the neck came later — and from other hands.

Months later, somewhere in Sector 4, Victor Rossi reopens the Hotel Alvorada with the insurance money.
900:
You accuse Evelyn Pendelton. The bar log puts her twenty floors away at the time of the crime, paying for drinks every ten minutes.

Her lawyers laugh. The corporation, embarrassed, revokes your license and closes the case.

Detective Vance hands back his badge in the acid rain. The killer was never found.

But Tomás was just a frightened witness. He heard the blow — he didn't strike it.

The real killer watches the trial on the hotel's holo-TV, adjusting the glove on his mechanical arm.
